_comment: Worked example for a fictional shop app. Every file fact points at a file under assets/example/repo, so build it with --repo assets/example/repo and the facts verify on any machine.
name: cache-port-example

epic.title: Cache access behind one port (worked example)
epic.goal: Every cache read and write in the shop app goes through one port, so a page can be cached and tested without environment variables or module state.
exit_criteria: `git grep "from shop.cache import" -- shop` matches only the adapter.
A deploy of the port returns the same pages as before.

scenarios.title: Behaviour is unchanged
given: the test suite before the change
then: it passes without edits to the expectations

scenarios.title: The old import path keeps working until it is retired
given: code that still imports the old path
then: it works through a re-export that a later story removes

scenarios.title: Tests follow the code
given: tests that import the moved code
then: they are updated in the same pull request
no test is left skipped

features.title: The cache port
features.goal: A CachePort with an in-process adapter exists and behaves like today's functions.
features.why: shop/cache.py is module-level state, so code that uses it cannot be tested without setting an environment variable first.
exit_criteria: The port and the adapter have unit tests that need no environment variable.

features.title: Adopt the port
features.goal: The handlers and reports use the port and the old functions are gone.
features.why: Until callers move the port is unused.
exit_criteria: No module outside the adapter imports the old functions.

stories.title: Define the CachePort and keep the in-process store as its adapter
stories.role: a developer adding a cached page
stories.want: a CachePort with get, set and invalidate-by-prefix, with the current in-process store as its first adapter
stories.so: a page can be cached and tested without environment variables or module state
stories.context: `shop/cache.py` is switched on by the `CACHE_ENABLED` environment variable and turns every operation into a no-op when it is off. The port must keep that behaviour.

facts.claim: every cache operation is a no-op unless CACHE_ENABLED is 1
invalidation removes every key that starts with a prefix and returns how many were removed

scenarios.title: The in-process adapter keeps entries until they expire
when: I set a key with a time to live of 1 second and read it back
I read it again after 2 seconds
then: the first read returns the value
the second read is a miss

scenarios.title: A disabled cache does nothing and does not fail
when: I call get and set through the port
then: get returns `None` and set returns `False`
the caller computes the value and no error is raised

scenarios.title: Prefix invalidation removes only matching keys
given: keys cached under the prefixes `report:` and `product:`
then: the `report:` keys are removed
the `product:` keys remain
the number of keys removed is returned

stories.design: A CachePort protocol in shop/ports.py; the in-process adapter wraps today's functions.

stories.title: Prove the cache behaves the same behind the port
stories.role: an operator deploying a new version
stories.want: a behaviour test that makes the same calls on the old functions and on the port
stories.so: a deploy never changes what a cached page returns
stories.context: `cache_set` stores a value for 300 seconds unless a time to live is given, and returns `False` when the cache is disabled.

facts.claim: the default time to live is 300 seconds
cache_set returns False when the cache is disabled
facts.quote: Returns False when the cache is disabled.

scenarios.title: Old and new agree on every call
when: I call <call> on the old functions and on the port
then: both return <result>

scenarios.title: A difference blocks the change
given: a port whose set returns `None` when the cache is enabled
then: it fails and names the call
the pull request cannot merge

scenarios.title: The default time to live is kept
given: a value set without a time to live
when: it is read after 299 seconds and again after 301 seconds
then: the first read is a hit
the second read is a miss

stories.title: Repoint the handlers and reports to the port
stories.role: a developer who wants no module to import the cache functions directly
stories.want: the product page, the search page and the reports to use the CachePort
stories.so: the cache can be replaced or faked in one place
stories.context: `shop/routes.py` and `shop/reports.py` import the cache functions directly and build their own keys (`product:{id}`, `search:{query}`, `report:sales:{day}`).

facts.claim: the handlers import cache_get and cache_set directly
the reports import the three cache functions directly
facts.quote: from shop.cache import cache_get, cache_invalidate, cache_set

facts.claim: only the handlers and the reports import the cache functions
facts.source: git grep -l "from shop.cache import" -- shop (20 Oct)

scenarios.title: No handler imports the old module
given: the port and the adapter from S1.1
when: I run `git grep "from shop.cache import" -- shop`
then: only the adapter matches

scenarios.title: Pages are unchanged
given: the product page, the search page and the sales report, with the cache enabled and disabled
when: they are called before and after the change
then: their responses are equal
the cache keys are identical (S1.2)

scenarios.title: Refreshing reports still removes only report keys
given: cached reports and cached product pages
then: every `report:` key is removed
the product pages remain cached

stories.design: Each module receives the port through its constructor or a function argument; key construction stays where it is.

technical_background.current_state: The two page handlers call the cache functions directly and build their own keys.

evidence.claim: the handlers import cache_get and cache_set from the module

technical_background.approach: Pass the port into `product_page` and `search_page`; keep the key construction identical.
technical_background.test_plan: Page tests before and after; a fake port records the calls and the keys.
technical_background.risks: Low: two call sites. Roll back by reverting the pull request.

technical_background.current_state: The reports call the cache functions directly and clear every report key after the nightly import.

evidence.claim: refresh_reports drops every cached report with a prefix

technical_background.approach: Pass the port into `sales_report` and `refresh_reports`; keep the `report:` prefix.
technical_background.test_plan: A report test that checks the keys written and the keys removed by `refresh_reports`.
technical_background.risks: Medium: invalidation must still remove only the `report:` keys.

stories.title: Remove the module-level cache functions
stories.role: a developer who reads the cache code
stories.want: `shop/cache.py` reduced to the in-process adapter, with the module-level functions removed
stories.so: there is one way to use the cache
stories.context: After S2.1 only the adapter should import the old functions.

scenarios.title: Only the adapter imports the old functions
when: I run `git grep "from shop.cache import" -- shop`
then: only the adapter matches

scenarios.title: The deletion stands alone
then: it contains only the removal of the old functions and re-exports

scenarios.title: The revert is rehearsed
then: the old functions return and the callers work

open_questions.question: Does the nightly import job outside this repository also import the old functions?
